g.text: Crooks use ready-made exploits within weeks, but

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #121212

g.text: take years to adopt new tools and business models
Time from a technology becoming available to widespread criminal use, log scale
New tools fit existing criminal work; business models need a new market, payment system or infrastructure. Classes were assigned
knowing the outcomes, and the cases were hand-picked, so medians are illustrative. Amber: AI. As a business model, AI agents
running whole intrusions have about a one-in-three chance of being widespread by the end of 2029; as a new tool, one in two.
Sources: Young and Yung (1996); FinCEN; Coveware; Chainalysis; Soska and Christin (USENIX 2015); Microsoft; Proofpoint;
Cloudflare; Wikipedia; Krebs on Security; Verizon DBIR; Palo Alto Networks Unit 42; Anthropic and Google threat reports; author's
Bayesian censored log-normal model (shading: 80% credible interval of each group's median)
